A distinct second pass compared all 240 question wordings with the saved rationales and source scope. Rechecked incumbent Lai Ching-te and relevant 2026 implemented actions. Distinguished amended legal texts from announcements and uncommenced provisions, including the July 2026 virtual-asset statute, professional-residence changes, August 2026 psychiatric court review, 2026 benefit increases and July 2026 Siraya recognition. Corrected rent-setting from mixed to market-leaning because enforcing an agreed rent is not general price control; changed public-rental ownership to mixed to exclude privately owned subsidised leases; withdrew inheritance-tax income-support linkage as unproven; supported unilateral tariff-reduction inference with an actual time-limited measure; replaced vague ceremony inference with the implemented Siraya ceremony; strengthened attention interaction evidence without treating research funding as adoption. Neutral answers represent stated conditional or mixed institutions. BTI 2026 covers February 2023 to January 2025 and is historical institutional corroboration, not evidence for later acts. Freedom House and Amnesty provide independent counterevidence. Review priorities for a separate agent: national-alliance delegation versus practical cooperation (nationalism 04), clinical explanations versus national causal belief (culture 01/04/09/11/12), permanent marine footprint inference (innovation 03/06), embryo laboratory work versus reproductive trials (innovation 13), and university graduation route versus automatic residence (immigration 12).
